entry.title: Holistic lithography: Optimizing chipmaking from design to mass production | ASML

media:group.media:title: Holistic lithography: Optimizing chipmaking from design to mass production | ASML
media:group.media:description:
Developing a chip from design to mass production is one of the most complex challenges in semiconductor manufacturing.
Holistic lithography helps chipmakers optimize and control that process from start to finish. By combining computational lithography, optical metrology, e-beam inspection and lithography systems, ASML enables customers to improve patterning performance, process stability and yield.
In this video, discover how chipmakers use holistic lithography to understand, optimize and control their patterning processes, from early design and process development to high-volume manufacturing. Learn how computational modeling, optical measurement, inspection and advanced control systems work together to help meet increasingly demanding patterning requirements for advanced chip technologies.
As semiconductor innovation continues to drive 2D scaling, 3D integration and new device architectures, holistic lithography helps chipmakers achieve the performance they need, on time and at the right cost.

entry.title: Why is the wafer stage important in High NA EUV lithography? | ASML

media:group.media:title: Why is the wafer stage important in High NA EUV lithography? | ASML
media:group.media:description:
In this video, Greet Storms, head of product management for High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography at ASML, walks you through the wafer stage’s pivotal role in advanced chipmaking. You’ll see two wafer tables magnetically levitating, a robotic arm loading a wafer through the vacuum load lock and a wafer getting electrostatically clamped in place.
Discover how advanced alignment sensors map specific markers on the wafer to position it accurately for lithography, while leveling sensors create an exact map of the wafer’s topology. Watch EUV light – carrying the pattern for a chip layer – get focused by multilayer mirrors we developed with ZEISS. See the light scan across the wafer in an S-shape to expose the chip pattern in just seconds.
Learn how the wafer stage in High NA EUV lithography enables ultra-fast and hyper-precise positioning for mass-producing the world’s most advanced microchips.

entry.title: What does the reticle stage do in High NA EUV lithography? | ASML

media:group.media:title: What does the reticle stage do in High NA EUV lithography? | ASML
media:group.media:description:
What role does the reticle stage play in High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography?
In this video, Greet Storms, head of product management for High NA EUV at ASML, explains how the reticle stage enables patterning in advanced chipmaking. You’ll see how 13.5 nanometer EUV light reflected into the system gets shaped by the illuminator and how a chip pattern gets encoded into the light for lithography.
Discover how the reticle stage moves back and forth at high speed so EUV light can quickly scan across the reticle to encode the chip pattern into the light beam.
Learn about how a reticle stage that accelerates at 32g, which is 30 times faster than an F1 car, moves in perfect synchronization with the wafer stage. Follow the reticle stage in action and see how it supports High NA EUV lithography in enabling the next generation of semiconductor manufacturing.
